name: Healthcare — Care Coordination
description: A care-coordination agent summarises a patient's care history. A shared care-plan record references other patients' encounters; following that reference is the realistic misstep the demo shows getting caught.
incident_headline: In 2025, security researchers demonstrated indirect prompt injection against a clinical AI system. A malicious instruction was embedded in a patient intake form — not visible to the clinician, just text in a field the agent would process. When the agent read the form, it followed the embedded instruction and began querying patient records outside the active encounter.
closing_line: HIPAA doesn't care whether it was a human or an agent that accessed the wrong patient record. AIControl makes that accountability automatic — and provable.

steps.label: Read the shared care plan for the assigned patient
steps.narrative: The care plan references a household member's shared intake encounter — that reference is what the agent follows next.

decision_narratives.allow: Authorized PHI access within active encounter scope. Logged.

steps.label: Fetch encounter for PT-2024-098234 — not the coordinator's assigned patient
steps.narrative: Following the care plan's household-member reference leads the agent to a different patient's encounter — cross-encounter PHI access outside this coordinator's assignment.

decision_narratives.deny: Blocked. That patient's record was never accessed. If your Privacy Officer gets a complaint tomorrow, this is your proof: attempted, blocked by policy, no access occurred.

steps.label: Fetch the assigned patient's own encounter
steps.narrative: The coordinator's actual job: summarising the assigned patient's own encounter. Allow.

decision_narratives.allow: Care summary for the assigned patient completed. Logged.
